    Sources indicate that uscreen is the video monetization platform for businesses building recurring revenue from video content. Our customers replace a patchwork stack of separate hosting, community, courses, email, and app vendors with one branded experience across web, mobile, and TV.

    Industry observers note that the platform is only half of it. We believe growth requires behavior, not just software. Customers don't stall because a feature is missing. They stall because they priced wrong, never built an email list, or introduced an offer nobody wanted. Coaching is how we fix that, and it's part of the product rather than an add-on.

    You own a segment, and you run it like a growth marketer.

    Industry observers note that we have a cohort of smaller video businesses where retention is not where it should be. Nobody owns it today. You will. The revenue that stays in that segment, and the revenue that grows inside it, is yours.

    In a recent development, this is a coaching role for someone with a growth marketer's mindset. We wouldn't hire a demand gen marketer who couldn't analyze the state of the business and figure out what's needed, and we won't hire a coach who can't either. You'll look at a customer's business the way an owner would: where the revenue comes from, where it leaks, and what to do next. You pull your own numbers to get there. When a customer needs a custom report to answer a growth question, you build it yourself.

    Industry observers note that it's a one-to-many job. Your cohort is larger than a 1:1 book, so the work is designing coaching that scales: cohort programs, group sessions, office hours, and triggered outreach when the data claims a business is drifting. You'll build that motion rather than inherit it.

    Success is measured in dollars: gross revenue retention in your cohort first, expansion second. Not tickets closed, not calls booked.

    A coach with a growth marketer's mindset. Maybe you've run growth or demand gen for a small business, built your own audience, or coached founders through their numbers. You understand how a membership business makes money, you pull your own analytics to see what's working, and you're comfortable doing it in front of a client. What matters is that you can find the real constraint in a business, then sit with the operator and say the honest thing.

    Why Mobile Apps Treasure Downtime; Terms Of Non-Endearment

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adexchanger

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mobile games compete with social media and streaming for attention in the cutthroat worlds of viral feeds and app marketplaces.
    • But wouldn’t it make more sense for these apps to compete for consumers’ downtime?
    • People using apps like DoorDash and Uber, for instance, “have nothing to do while they wait,” as Braberg puts it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mobile games compete with social media and streaming for attention in the cutthroat worlds of viral feeds and app marketplaces.

    But wouldn’t it make more sense for these apps to compete for consumers’ downtime? That’s the case made by Felix Braberg, a mobile ad and monetization consultant, in a blog post.

    People using apps like DoorDash and Uber, for instance, “have nothing to do while they wait,” as Braberg puts it. Meanwhile, both DoorDash and Uber have billion-dollar annual ad businesses, but they’re not rushing to build their own gaming or streaming offerings. So they’re natural fits for app advertisers looking to help users pass the time.

    Recent findings suggest that appLovin’s strength in mobile gaming is not so dissimilar. But AppLovin has a nascent consumer advertising segment now, and a few of its early advertisers have noted the power of reaching people while they’re playing games on the toilet. It doesn’t get more “downtime” than that.

    According to recent reports, gaming can fit neatly into the downtime vacuum that right now is awkwardly filled by ads or nothing. But successfully advertising a mobile game traditionally required a user to download the game and leave the app where they saw it advertised.

    Now, though, startups such as PlaysOut are integrating mobile games directly into other apps and monetizing those experiences with rewarded video. It’s a way for nongaming apps to capitalize on the downtime that benefits gaming.

    Which leads Braberg to predict that the next wave of mobile growth “will come from apps that were never game companies.”.

    Scarcely a week after launching ChatGPT’s fresh Business Hub, designed to let businesses see how they’re performing in ChatGPT, OpenAI has revised the Hub’s terms of service, Digiday reports.

    The revisions came soon after Digiday reached out to OpenAI, citing legal concerns brought forward by lawyers on behalf of publishers.

    Industry observers note that some of those legal restrictions have been removed in the revised terms of service. However, the revised terms also introduced more restrictions, such as requiring companies to waive their right to seek a court order preventing OpenAI from using certain customer data.

    According to recent reports, but, while OpenAI is still imposing some legal restrictions on companies that use its Business Hub, “they don’t leave a customer completely without recourse,” an IP and tech lawyer who requested anonymity tells Digiday. “A customer could still, even if not entirely practical, sue for monetary damages.”.

    In a recent development, the Italian conglomerate Bending Spoons has been amassing a collection of consumer- and business-facing software vendors that kind of resembles the Island of Misfit Toys. It added another dud (or stud?) to its stable last week.

    Bending Spoons will acquire Mailchimp from Intuit for about $3.7 billion, less than a third of what Intuit paid a decade ago, Reuters reports.

    Bending Spoons also recently added the online whiteboard Miro and location-based pet-tracking service Tractive, plus once-promising internet companies Brightcove, Evernote, Meetup, Vimeo and AOL. Its business model is akin to private equity, in that it acquires struggling companies and drastically reduces headcount while raising prices or removing free tiers. Interestingly, advertising is an ancillary part of its model.

    In a recent development, to be clear, AOL and Vimeo haven’t quit on ad revenue. But Bending Spoons is focused on subscription revenue growth and consolidated cost savings, rather than building an identity spine for advertising and data sales.

    Sources indicate that but Bending Spoons still must demonstrate that it can turn flatlined businesses (Mailchimp declined year over year, for instance) into earners. Which is a bit like trying to bend a spoon using only your mind.

    Great news on the turnaround front: Bending Spoons reported 125% revenue growth last week.

    It has been revealed that but there’s some not-so-great news, too: Its organic growth was an anemic 3%. So growth is coming from net-new businesses, with these acquisitions contributing some $4 billion in debt.

    #158570. The Trade Desk Can Win Again By Embracing Objectivity And Letting Go Of The Open Web

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1056 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 Adexchanger ↗ Open Full Page

    The Trade Desk Can Win Again By Embracing Objectivity And Letting Go Of The Open Web

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1056 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adexchanger

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, wall Street loves to pile on ad tech.
    • No manufacturer has felt the highs and lows of being public quite like The Trade Desk (TTD), which, outside of AppLovin and the Magnificent 7, is the best company to emerge from the ad tech sector in the last 25 years.
    • According to recent reports, TTD was built on a brilliant principle: that brands and agencies should be able to decide where their media dollars go without the manufacturer selling the media sitting in the room.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, wall Street loves to pile on ad tech. They’re all about you when you’re up and quick to dismiss you when you’re down.

    No manufacturer has felt the highs and lows of being public quite like The Trade Desk (TTD), which, outside of AppLovin and the Magnificent 7, is the best company to emerge from the ad tech sector in the last 25 years.

    According to recent reports, TTD was built on a brilliant principle: that brands and agencies should be able to decide where their media dollars go without the manufacturer selling the media sitting in the room. That idea remains true, and it is the reason TTD became the largest independent DSP in the world.

    It has been revealed that so what changed? TTD latched onto a fresh principle: the defense of the open internet. Which means the company built its core value prop around a shrinking portion of where consumers spend their time and where advertisers spend their money.

    As DV360 became Google’s Death Star, The Trade Desk was the Rebel Alliance standing up for the open web. But while TTD spent the last several years proving they were the anti-Google, Amazon snuck in the back door and changed the whole DSP market.

    Recent findings suggest that if The Trade Desk holds to its first principle and lets go of the second, its value becomes more obvious than ever. Three moves would signal a upcoming era for the company:.

    1. Separate the value prop of “open internet” with objective decisioning. The tech giant should retire the open internet as its stated purpose and replace it with what all advertisers value: independent, data-driven decisioning for brands and agencies. The open web stays in the portfolio as one channel among several, allowing buyers to see the whole field.

    Industry observers note that 2. Offer an objective view of the walled gardens. Google will not let a third-party DSP bid on YouTube, and Meta has shown no interest in opening its auction. But neither fact prevents The Trade Desk from ingesting platform reporting, independent measurement and content data from nearly every walled garden, then normalizing it against its own CTV and open web buys.

    Sources indicate that 3. Save the open internet by showing the whole picture. TTD taking an objective view of all platforms would highlight measurement and quality discrepancies. Which would, in turn, improve the open internet’s reputation in the eyes of the buy side. Without that full view, there is no way to show how “premium” open internet performs against the largest user-generated platforms in the world.

    Industry observers note that from the beginning, The Trade Desk owned no inventory at all. It had no financial reason to steer a dollar anywhere except where the data mentioned it would work for the buyer.

    TTD’s 2016 S-1 organized the firm’s strengths under headings like “We Do Not Arbitrage Advertising Inventory” and “We Are Data-Driven.” The phrase “open internet” does not appear in the company’s prospectus summary or risk factors at all.

    The business built on that positioning worked extremely well. TTD went public in September 2016, grew revenue from $308 million in 2017 to $2.44 billion in 2024, reached a market cap of roughly $40 billion by 2021 and met or beat expectations for 33 consecutive quarters.

    Industry observers note that in 2025, growth slowed and stock performance followed suit. That slowing growth is the natural effect of being the Pied Piper of the shrinking “open web.”.

    Sources indicate that redseer Strategy Consultants estimate that the programmatic open web gets only 20%-30% of ad budgets, with 70%-80% of programmatic spend going to walled gardens. This split has held for roughly five years.

    Advertisers have already made their decision. Budgets did not follow time spent, because walled gardens offer simplicity that programmatic cannot: an easy button for efficient reach. While the value of that reach can be debated, the easy way won.

    The concentration of spend is still increasing. EMarketer expects Google, Meta and Amazon to take 62.3% of worldwide digital ad spend in 2026, with Meta at about $243 billion and Google at about $240 billion. Amazon is forecast to grow from $69 billion in 2025 to $97 billion in 2027. Every incremental dollar in those forecasts is a dollar that an independent DSP cannot bid on today. Forecasts are growing faster than the open web.

    Recent findings suggest that television was supposed to be the market where the “open internet” reclaimed ground with upper-funnel brands. Except CTV is also becoming a walled garden medium. In Nielsen’s May 2026 Gauge, YouTube accounted for 13.8% of all US TV viewing, making Google the single largest media distributor in the US.

    Advertisers have limited transparency into the AI products of each walled garden. The content itself is UGC (and increasingly AI-generated). The measurement is dictated by the platform. And yet marketers need to spend there in order to get reach and efficiency. Imagine if there were a truly objective way to spend those dollars?

    Industry observers note that none of this means that TTD’s founding principle failed. It means the principle is aimed at an open web target that keeps getting smaller. An objective buyer that can only see 20%-30% of the budget is no longer willing to spend the time, money and energy on the shrinking pie.

    In a recent development, CMOs have one budget. The question they actually want answered is where the next dollar should go across YouTube, Meta, TikTok, Snap, CTV and the web, backed by objective data. Today, nobody independently answers that question. The Trade Desk is the only company in the industry that is poised to provide a solution.

    According to recent reports, most turnarounds require a company to find a latest reason to exist, and most of them fail because the new reason is never as convincing as the original one. This turnaround just requires The Trade Desk to remember its original reason for being.

    When The Trade Desk opens up its view beyond the open web, Wall Street – and the buy side – will rejoice.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    Supabase is the backend of choice for a growing wave of AI-native builders, and we're deepening structured partnerships with the platforms they build on top of — Anthropic, OpenAI, Vercel, and Lovable. These partners' teams are talking to thousands of developers and agents who need exactly what we build—a full backend platform with Postgres at the core—without the vendor lock-in. This is an opportunity to get Supabase in front of the right partner SAs and make us the default recommendation for a modern, AI-ready backend.

    We’re looking for a Platform Solutions Architect to join our Success Team and help embed Supabase into the Solutions and Engineering communities with AI Builders.

    You’ll work closely with Partner Solutions Architects and Partner Engineers at Anthropic, OpenAI, Vercel, and Lovable, helping us proactively identify builder problems where Supabase is the right solution and closing the gap between partner intent and real developer outcomes. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions of AI-native apps and agents.

    In this role, you’ll focus on three core pillars:.

    Build deep relationships with Technical counterparts at Anthropic, OpenAI, Vercel, and Lovable, focusing initially on defined use cases and agent/app-migration motions.

    Develop and deliver technical workshops, training materials, and enablement content to give partner SAs the fluency to position Supabase.

    Create demos, integration guides, and reference architectures that make Supabase’s fit with Anthropic, OpenAI, Vercel, and Lovable immediately legible.

    Partner with SAs at these companies on active opportunities to move deals forward and feeding technical pipeline intelligence back to the alliance lead.

    Resolve blockers for partner SAs working on Supabase implementations to maintain their credibility with the builders they support.

    Troubleshoot complex integration scenarios and turn solutions into reusable assets.

    Maintain a close feedback loop with Supabase product and engineering teams to ensure technical guidance reflects the latest platform capabilities.

    Measure success through co-sell opportunities sourced, influenced deals, and SA enablement metrics across the Anthropic, OpenAI, Vercel, and Lovable partnerships.

    Write technical blog posts and case studies that demonstrate real-world Supabase implementations built on Anthropic, OpenAI, Vercel, and Lovable.

    Recent findings suggest that represent Supabase at conferences, meetups, and partner-sponsored events (e.g. Anthropic and OpenAI dev days, Vercel Ship, Lovable community events).

    Develop video content and interactive learning experiences to reduce the "time-to-fluency" for partner SAs.

    In a recent development, have 5+ years of experience in technical roles with deep hands-on experience building on modern AI infrastructure. Previous experience working at Anthropic, OpenAI, Vercel, Lovable (or a similar AI builder platform) or as a partner to one is required.

    Understand how partner SAs at AI builder platforms are incentivized, how they make recommendations, and how the partner ecosystem influences developer decisions.

    Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences, explaining complex concepts with ease.

    Have a strong technical foundation in PostgreSQL, APIs, and modern development frameworks like React and Next.js, plus fluency with AI/agent tooling (LLM APIs, MCP, agent frameworks).

    Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving quickly to build a playbook from scratch.

    Are energized by solving real-world problems for developers building the next generation of AI-native products.

    According to recent reports, we hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    Industry observers note that every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the manufacturer. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are vital to us.

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a fresh city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    It has been revealed that supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    In a recent development, we move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

    #158563. AI Needs To Cite Its Sources. This Consumer Intelligence Platform Ensures It Does

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (687 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Adexchanger ↗ Open Full Page

    AI Needs To Cite Its Sources. This Consumer Intelligence Platform Ensures It Does

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (687 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adexchanger

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • When Stravito was launched roughly nine years ago, its goal was to help brands put the right product in front of the right consumer early in their shopping journey.
    • Now, in the age of generative AI, its focus hasn’t changed so much as its structure and execution.
    • At the crux of the company is “the idea of bringing your strategy to life,” CEO and Founder Thor Olof Philogène told AdExchanger.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When Stravito was launched roughly nine years ago, its goal was to help brands put the right product in front of the right consumer early in their shopping journey.

    Now, in the age of generative AI, its focus hasn’t changed so much as its structure and execution. Stravito, which touts itself as a consumer intelligence platform, uses AI to help marketers better understand their customers’ preferences and predict their reactions to ads.

    At the crux of the company is “the idea of bringing your strategy to life,” CEO and Founder Thor Olof Philogène told AdExchanger.

    Indeed, it’s the crux of the firm name: Stravito is a portmanteau of the words “strategy” and “vito,” which comes from the Latin word for life, “vita.”.

    In September, it launched its AI Persona Builder product, which uses brands’ data to develop AI personas that reflect their audiences.

    Stravito connects to a brand’s first-party data as well as other sources, like surveys and syndicated research, plus Stravito’s data from prior campaigns. From there, it builds out different AI personas for different audiences. The personas can represent smaller, more niche audiences, like people from a specific geo to capture “regional nuances,” said Philogène, or broader audiences, like millennials or Gen Z. Marketers can ask a persona a specific question, like why they prefer one version of an ad over another, “and get instant feedback,” he added.

    Coffee brand Lavazza, for instance, conducted several thousand consumer interviews that it was able to integrate into the personas it built with Stravito. When Lavazza was testing different styles of packaging for its Dolcevita line of coffee, it was able to get feedback on the different variations from a relevant customer persona.

    Sources indicate that for this particular launch, Lavazza tested its US audience persona, which was built on data, including roughly 5,000 consumer interviews conducted through Kantar and research by the National Coffee Association. The research “covered consumers’ broader attitudes toward life, not only their attitudes toward coffee,” remarked Philogène, which helped with aesthetic decisions.

    Sources indicate that based on the persona’s responses to the colors and other visual cues, Lavazza ultimately changed the packaging color from black to dark blue, Philogène remarked. It then validated the decision by testing the new designs on Meta and comparing engagement.

    Industry observers note that but rather than just spitting out recommendations and hoping that marketers will trust the personas’ responses at face value, Stravito takes a “glass box” approach to AI, remarked Philogène. This means that every suggestion and piece of feedback that the AI generates is accompanied by the specific sources and citations that informed it.

    Industry observers note that when your boss asks why you’re making a certain investment, “you do not want to tell them, you know, because AI told me so,” quipped Philogène. Instead, Stravito backs up its decision with the data sources it’s connected to.

    Recent findings suggest that but no matter how much research a brand or tech vendor has access to, no AI tool can accurately answer every question that someone may pose. And Stravito is exceedingly aware of that. Before a user even asks a question, stated Philogène, the AI persona will note topics that it doesn’t have enough data to answer questions about, such as a brand’s pricing model.

    Sources indicate that an AI tool’s lack of knowledge can be “a feature, not a bug,” said Philogène. It’s crucial for brands to understand what data they’re lacking and where they should commission extra data, he added.

    Stravito’s AI “won’t be sycophantic” and just tell consumers what they want to hear, stated Philogène. (Take that, ChatGPT.) Rather, it first determines whether or not it has enough data to answer a given question, and if it does, it specifies whether the answer is explicitly stated in the original source versus inferred. That way, the user can understand the logic backing up every one of the model’s conclusions.

    Having the necessary sources to back up one’s claims and decisions is a crucial facet of journalism, law and research, Philogène said. Shouldn’t advertising be held to the same standard?

    GTA VI is smashing Twitch’s records—and it wants to make sure advertisers don’t miss out

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (473 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Grand Theft Auto fans across the world are still eagerly anticipating Rockstar’s long-awaited sequel to roll out in their regions.
    • As of publication time, GTA VI has attracted a peak of 3.29 million concurrent viewers on Twitch, 3.19M on YouTube, and 1.5M on Kick.Those totals put it “ahead of every previous game launch tracked by Streams Charts,” the data firm said in its report.
    • Industry observers note that twitch isn’t taking all that buzz—or the dollar signs that come with it—for granted.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Grand Theft Auto fans across the world are still eagerly anticipating Rockstar’s long-awaited sequel to roll out in their regions. But according to data from Streams Charts, GTA VI has already smashed multiple streaming platform records—including becoming “the most popular gaming category in Twitch history by peak viewers.”.

    As of publication time, GTA VI has attracted a peak of 3.29 million concurrent viewers on Twitch, 3.19M on YouTube, and 1.5M on Kick.Those totals put it “ahead of every previous game launch tracked by Streams Charts,” the data firm said in its report.

    Industry observers note that twitch isn’t taking all that buzz—or the dollar signs that come with it—for granted. But GTA also doesn’t exactly fit into the platform’s careful approach to brand safety. So, it’s introducing new tech to ensure that advertisers can cash in on the hype surrounding GTA VI without putting their brand reputations at risk.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Back in September, Twitch CEO Dan Clancy told hosts of The Snarketing Podcast that the platform had begun using AI to evaluate whether streamers are squeaky-clean enough for brands to run ads against their content.

    Recent findings suggest that “[W]e transcribe streams to figure out ‘Is this appropriate for this brand?’” he said. “So that’s something that we’ve had to invest a lot in to make sure that for a brand, their content is appearing next to creators and content that fits what they’re trying to do.”.

    That enhancement didn’t come out of nowhere: Twitch has long asked streamers to label their content in certain circumstances where mature themes or imagery are involved.

    As Gizmodo noted, this means creators have historically missed out on ad revenue when streaming mature-rated games, “because while streamers can receive donations from viewers, significant-time monetization ultimately depends on advertising, and advertisers are generally skittish around things that might frighten the poor sensitive product-buying public.”.

    Last week, however, Clancy told Bloomberg‘s Romaine Bostick that “one of the challenges in this space is advertisers want to be part of the GTA 6 launch”—they just don’t want their ads to appear alongside the spicier parts of the game.

    To solve that problem, Twitch’s latest technology will allow brands to run ads on GTA VI streams while also ensuring that (as Clancy phrased it) “any of the parts of GTA 6 that they might not want to have their ads associated with, their ads won’t be associated with that.”.

    According to recent reports, the ins and outs of how that system will actually work remain to be seen. But if it does prove effective for GTA VI, we’ll be watching to see whether Twitch expands the tech to other streams and genres previously dismissed as unsafe for brands.

    Another Disney creator deal: YouTube illusionist Zach King joins the Mouse House

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (523 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Disney continues to prove that Netflix isn’t the only competitor sniffing around YouTube‘s top talent.
    • Recent findings suggest that for their deal, 36-year-old L.A.-based King will make 10 original short-form videos, which Disney will have exclusive rights to distribute.
    • Recent findings suggest that one of the King projects coming to Disney+ is Cardboard Wars, his 52-minute intentionally-low-budget tribute to Star Wars: A New Hope.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Disney continues to prove that Netflix isn’t the only competitor sniffing around YouTube‘s top talent.

    Recent findings suggest that for their deal, 36-year-old L.A.-based King will make 10 original short-form videos, which Disney will have exclusive rights to distribute. Disney notes the agreement “will also bring [King’s] signature illusions to newly introduced content for Disney+ and [King’s] own channels inspired by Disney’s Hexed, Star Wars, and other Disney films and experiences.”.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Recent findings suggest that one of the King projects coming to Disney+ is Cardboard Wars, his 52-minute intentionally-low-budget tribute to Star Wars: A New Hope. King uploaded the film to YouTube in August, and soon will cross-post it to Disney’s streaming service.

    A post shared by Zach King (@zachking).

    But there’s still more: King will pop up on Disney’s social accounts as well, hosting behind-the-scenes content about the VFX and filmmaking techniques he uses in his content.

    Sources indicate that “I fell in love with filmmaking and storytelling as a young kid, grabbing my parents’ home video camera and teaching myself to edit,” King wrote in an Instagram post. “A lot of my early homemade films were inspired by the Disney movies and the behind-the-scenes footage they would show in the DVD featurettes. There was always a sense of magic I would see on the screen, and so I’m thrilled to be working with Disney to continue that magic of filmmaking for the next generation of storytellers.”.

    Industry observers note that king has worked with Disney regularly in recent months: He was at its glitzy Created in L.A. event in September, and earlier this month played a game of viral format Cake or Fake? with Hexed (and Arcane, and Sinners, and Spider-Verse, and Hawkeye) star Hailee Steinfeld. But this is his first official, expansive content deal.

    “Zach makes the impossible look real, bringing the kind of imagination and originality that has always defined Disney,” Asad Ayaz, The Walt Disney Company’s CMO and Brand Officer, noted in a statement. “He brings both a filmmaker’s ingenuity and a fan’s passion to our stories, along with a unique connection with audiences. We want to build lasting relationships with creators like Zach, giving their ideas room to grow across Disney. That’s what makes this next chapter of our work together so full of possibility.”.

    As we mentioned above, everyone–including YouTube–has had their eye on Netflix’s obvious poaching efforts…leaving room for Disney to sneak in the back.

    In the last couple months, Disney has unveiled deals with major creators Dhar Mann, Dude Perfect, and Like Nastya. Crucially, these are all development deals–the exact kind of agreement that has YouTube on guard with Netflix.

    Recent findings suggest that and Disney’s not quite showing its full hand just yet. During its earnings call Nov. 17, executives only mentioned YouTubers once, in passing and in reference to Disney+’s growing crop of approved creator content.

    We suspect more is in the pipeline–and that YouTube may have to start paying creators to turn down Disney deals, too.

    This isn’t another product job.

    It’s the chance to define a upcoming category : The Operating System (OS) for Human Greatness Augmented with AI.

    Science-backed. Design-led. AI-powered. Global.

    A chance to build an AI-native Product Department.

    You’ll be working with the most complex data in the world : the human mind.

    Deep inside you are looking for a new adventure with….

    🚀Ambition around AI field : Smart teammates driven to create an iconic, international product.

    🔥Impact : you strive to make a real difference in the tech giant's growth, and not be a number in a significant organization.

    😍Mission : knowing your greatness left a mark in people's lives, through technology and behavioral science.

    At Paradox, we believe that greatness is trainable.

    That’s why we want to empower people at scale by leveraging cutting edge technologies like AI, and crafting user experiences with outstanding aesthetics.

    - Human Intelligence (coaches, peers, and mentors).

    - Structured Intelligence (protocols, mental models, rituals),.

    - Technological Intelligence (AI personalization, feedback loops, adaptive journeys).

    To create one seamless ecosystem: Paradox OS.

    This is why we are looking for a PM to make Paradox a category-defining global brand loved for its product.

    This is a full-time position from our beautiful offices in Dubai, Paris or Lisbon or remotely anywhere in the world.

    We believe self-help is broken.Most learning platforms are used the same way : consuming generic theories, getting quick highs, ending with no real change.

    At Paradox, we believe people deserve more.More than content. More than motivation.

    They deserve a system that knows them, one that adapts, challenges, and grows with them.

    We believe that every human learns differently, and that technology can do more than entertain or save time.It can translate insight into transformation, through AI personalization, lean experimentation, and deep psychological understanding.

    Because learning shouldn’t just make you feel inspired for a day, it should change how you live, think, and create.

    At Paradox, we want to re-invent how people grow.

    We do not build another course or coaching app but the Operating System for Greatness.

    Founded by David Laroche - a creator followed by over 2 million people and known for his interviews with icons like Tony Parker, Mike Horn, Richard Branson, and Gad Elmaleh, Paradox aims to build something that will live beyond any individual (including its founder), for decades to come.

    Our ambition is to compete with players like Mindvalley (150M ARR), but with a sharper vision, grounded protocols for achievers, people who want more for their life, refusing mediocrity.

    To do that, we bring together designers, tech, coaches, and filmmakers to create learning experiences that are cinematic, precise, and effective.

    In a recent development, we move fast, aim high, and hold ourselves to the standards of Apple, Spotify, and MasterClass. No fluff, focused on meaningful impact.

    While others hide their numbers, we want to let our results speak loudly for us.

    Get obsessed with transforming our clients’ lives and let those transformations be our marketing.

    We want to build an AI-native organization, with agents in every department doing the work alongside our people.

    In product, that means building a self-learning AI for product management: a system that learns from every user signal, experiment and release, and gets sharper at deciding what to build next.

    For our clients, it means a self-learning AI that serves them through psychology and coaching, and gets better at helping each person change with every interaction.

    You won’t just use AI tools: you’ll help design the agents, loops and feedback systems that make Paradox learn faster than anyone else.

    -----------------------------------------.

    As Product Manager, you’ll be the architect of a latest category, transforming growth into a living ecosystem powered by AI, behavioral science, and design.

    You won’t just build features, you’ll craft experiences that rewire behavior.

    You’re the architect bringing clarity between vision and execution, the person who turns “we should build this” into “it’s live, here’s the data and tangible impact.”.

    Every product cycle you lead will integrate:.

    Protocols : guided frameworks grounded in psychology that rewire perception, emotion, and action.

    Pods : human connection, accountability, and shared rituals.

    Loops : adaptive, AI-powered coaching cycles that evolve with each user.

    Personalization : experiences that feel uniquely theirs, every time.

    Recent findings suggest that going from a successful personal brand, to an international tech-driven iconic brand, is far from easy. It will be messy, chaotic - requiring constant iterations on MVPs and innovation in tech. Therefore to achieve this here are :.

    -----------------------------------------.

    Translate the founder’s strategic vision into a clear product strategy.

    Build and maintain the roadmap that connects business goals, user outcomes, and technological innovation.

    Ensure every feature supports the evolution of the Paradox ecosystem: Loops, PX Agents, Protocols, Membership.

    Be obsessed with user problems : talk to people weekly, analyze patterns, and identify where transformation breaks.

    Turn insights from behavioral science, coaching psychology, and learning design into actionable product hypotheses.

    Design loops, feedback, and rituals that make growth tangible.

    build for both the heart (inspiration) and the brain (structure).

    Apply Lean Startup methodology and scientific thinking to validate ideas through MVPs, not opinions.

    Design experiments and measurable success metrics before building.

    Iterate on a weekly basis on fresh hypothesis.

    Define and track product success metrics (activation, retention, transformation rates).

    Connect data to business KPIs, know how your product drives lifetime value, not just engagement.

    We don’t track metrics just for internal dashboards, we track them also to prove transformation.

    Help marketing leverage this data to fuel authentic, evidence-based storytelling — showing the world what real transformation looks like.

    Create a visceral experience that translates into emotions of inspiration, awe from users.

    Use a Science-backed, Cinematic, Contrarian style : Every product touchpoint should be grounded in behavioral science, expressed with cinematic beauty, and challenge conventions.

    -----------------------------------------.

    3–6 years as a Product Manager / Product Owner in EdTech, SaaS, or Consumer Tech.

    Bonus: experience in AI-driven products, learning design, or personal development platforms.

    You’ve shipped at least one major feature or product end-to-end, and can show measurable results.

    Uses Figma comfortably, prototypes directly.

    Craft-obsessed : You get things done, you love to work much beyond 9-5, you have a doer mentality, a bias for outcomes and want to be a beast in your field.

    User & Impact Obsessed: You think in outcomes, not outputs, you care about transformation.

    Analytical & System Thinker: You can turn a vague problem into a clear hypothesis, metrics, and roadmap.

    Digital & AI savvy : you’re able to build AI Agents (if not, you demonstrate ability to learn while applying).

    Cross-disciplinary Curiosity: You speak both tech and human; You can move from vision to spreadsheet to Figma.

    English: Fluent English, you can hold a conversation on specific details with English-speaking colleagues.

    Our chosen language for written communication is English.

    --------------------------------.

    ❌ If you need clarity before chaos — wrong place.❌ If you prefer balance over intensity — wrong season.❌ If you build to deliver, not to elevate — wrong mission.

    In a recent development, ❌Surface-level Vision Alignment : you like the idea of Paradox but doesn’t want to get the depth. Paradox is design-led; you must touch the product, not just manage it.

    ✅ If you’re obsessed with systems, psychology, and design…✅ If you dream of using AI to amplify what makes us human….

    Build a product that fuses neuroscience, design, and AI to reinvent how humans grow.

    The chance to build a product that could redefine human potential.

    Work with filmmakers, psychologists, engineers, and creatives obsessed with impact.

    In the heart of our headquarters stands the 100 000 Dreams Wall,.

    Every photo on that wall is a life rewritten:.

    “I found peace with my father.”.

    You will play a crucial role in the development of an Iconic Product.

    -> 🏅Being surrounded by A-players who strive to perform.

    But you don’t just want a competitive paycheck, you also want….

    -> Playing a crucial role in the development of a organization whose content and products will be used by millions of people.

    -> Waking up in the morning feeling like you are making a difference is something!We receive messages every day from clients who have successfully lost weight, quit smoking, reached a milestone in their business, built better relationships, and made positive changes in their lives.

    -> ❤️ Contributing to the Paradox Foundation (our non-profit), dedicated to empower teenagers.

    But that's not all, we believe that driven people deserve….

    -> 😎A organization culture based on autonomy & accountability.

    -> 🌎A remote culture from day one with the freedom to work from wherever you want.

    -> 🏤Magnificent office in Dubai, Paris, Lisbon - it feels like home :).

    -> 🧍‍♀️Standing desks paid by the tech giant if you live far from our offices.

    -> 💻Work on Mac, for us it counts :).

    -> 🏀350€ per year paid by the tech giant to take care of yourself ( for your gym, or dance class or whatever make you feel great).

    -> 📚150€ of books or education - At Paradox, we are learner lovers and we want to support you in that.

    -> 🔥6 1:1coachings - A Paradox Coach supporting you on anything personal or professional, we want you to live your best life.

    Industry observers note that ⚠️ To complete the recruitment process, each candidate must organize calls with his or her previous managers. If you are not comfortable with this : do not apply ⚠️.

    If all this sounds good to you, come and write the next chapter with us 🚀🚀🚀🚀.

    That job description resonated with you?

    Here is your tailor made hiring process.

    📃 A 6 to 8 minutes application survey (with a short video assignment).

    💻 A 30mn video call with Timy, HR, to deep dive into your career path and ambitions.

    💻 A 1h video call with Timy, HR, to discuss how you'd fit into Paradox’s Product team.

    💻 A 1h culture-fit video call, to assess alignment with our values and mindset.

    💻 A 1h final video call with David, CEO, to discuss Product Vision and the next milestones to build.

    💼 Reference check to understand how you operate across environments and help set you up for a smooth onboarding.

    Our recruitment process is tailored to do our best to avoid that you or us realize that we’re not a perfect fit. Every step serves a purpose and will allow us to get to know you better as much as it’ll help you understand more where you’ll be stepping in.

    We also want you to have time to ask all of your questions regarding the mission, the long-term vision of your team and the company, our values, with the relevant interlocutor in front of you.

    If you believe design and AI can awaken what’s best in us then this isn’t a career move.

    Let’s build the Operating System for Greatness.

    Robots.txt Guide – Best Practices For Search & AI Crawlers via @sejournal, @vahandev

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2691 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The robots.txt file has always been an essential tool for managing crawler access to a website.
    • Recent findings suggest that but, blocking the wrong bot can exclude your content from LLMs or SERPs, while leaving unnecessary URLs open can waste crawl budget on large sites.
    • This guide will help you understand how robots.txt rules work so you can avoid common robots.txt mistakes, keep useful content accessible, but at the same time limit unnecessary crawling.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The robots.txt file has always been an essential tool for managing crawler access to a website. With AI search tools and agents now visiting websites alongside traditional crawlers, you need to know which rules each one follows.

    Recent findings suggest that but, blocking the wrong bot can exclude your content from LLMs or SERPs, while leaving unnecessary URLs open can waste crawl budget on large sites. So, you need to know what you are doing.

    This guide will help you understand how robots.txt rules work so you can avoid common robots.txt mistakes, keep useful content accessible, but at the same time limit unnecessary crawling.

    The robots.txt is a simple text file that sits in the root directory of your site and tells crawlers what should be crawled.

    The table below provides a quick reference to the key robots.txt directives.

    This 2024 screenshot shows an example of robots.txt from ikea.com with multiple rules.

    Note that robots.txt doesn’t support full regular expressions and only has two wildcards:.

    Also, note that URL path matching is case-sensitive, e.g., “filter=” is not equal to “Filter=.” The directive names and user-agent matching are case-insensitive.

    When setting up a robots.txt file, it’s crucial to know the order in which search engines decide which rules to apply in case of conflicting rules.

    When you write a separate set of rules for a bot, it follows those rules instead of the rules under User-agent: *. For example:.

    It has been revealed that here, Googlebot can crawl /private/ because its own rules allow every URL to be crawled. To block that directory for Googlebot, add Disallow: /private/ beneath its Allow: / line.

    Within the applicable group, Google follows these two key rules:.

    The rule that matches more characters in the URL will be applied. For example:.

    In this case, the “Allow: /downloads/free/” rule is more specific than “Disallow: /downloads/” because it targets a subdirectory.

    Google will allow crawling of subfolder “/downloads/free/” but block everything else under “/downloads/.”.

    When multiple rules are equally specific, for example:.

    Google will choose the least restrictive one. This means Google will allow access to /downloads/.

    Google’s 2024 reminder about action URLs focused on add-to-cart and wishlist links that waste crawler and server resources.

    According to recent reports, imagine you have an online store with hundreds of thousands of pages. There are sections of websites like filtered pages that may have an infinite number of versions. Those pages don’t have unique value, essentially contain duplicate content, and may create infinite crawl space, thus wasting your server and Googlebot’s resources. That is where robots.txt comes in, preventing search engine bots from crawling those pages.

    If you don’t do that, Google may try to crawl an infinite number of URLs with different (even non-existent) search parameter values, causing spikes and a waste of crawl budget.

    As a general rule, you should always ask why certain pages exist, and whether they have any value for search engines to crawl and index.

    Depending on your site and indexing goals, candidates for crawl restrictions include:.

    Let’s dive into examples of how you can use robots.txt for each case.

    Sources indicate that internal search results are a common source of unnecessary crawling by Google and other search engines. If those results are not intended to appear in search, consider restricting their crawl space.

    On WordPress websites, it is usually an “s” parameter, and the URL looks like this:.

    Gary Illyes from Google has repeatedly warned to block “action” URLs as they can cause Googlebot to crawl them indefinitely even non-existent URLs with different combinations.

    Here is the rule you can use in your robots.txt to block such URLs from being crawled:.

    This crawl-stats screenshot, included in the original 2024 guide, illustrates reduced crawling of non-existent internal search URLs after they were blocked via robots.txt.

    In a recent development, note that Google may index blocked pages based on links to their URLs. Robots.txt does not guarantee their removal from search. If removal is your goal, use noindex and allow Google to crawl the page so it can read that instruction.

    Faceted navigation is an integral part of every ecommerce website. There can be cases where faceted navigation is part of an SEO strategy and aimed at ranking for general product searches.

    Zalando’s color-based landing pages, such as those targeting “gray t-shirt” illustrate this approach. The principle is to keep useful search landing pages crawlable while restricting unwanted filter combinations.

    However, in most cases, this is not the case, and filter parameters are used merely for filtering products, creating dozens of pages with duplicate content.

    According to recent reports, there may be multiple filter parameters in one URL. Identify which ones generate unwanted crawl space; do not block facets that form part of your search strategy. Google’s faceted-navigation guidance distinguishes these two cases.

    For example, if you have filters with the following parameters “sortby,” “color,” and “price,” you may use this set of rules:.

    These pairs match each parameter in the first position or after another parameter. Add only the parameters you intend to restrict, and test both wanted and unwanted URLs.

    UTM parameters are used for tracking purposes.

    According to recent reports, in the Reddit exchange shown below, John Mueller addressed tracking parameters on external links. Keep that context separate from internally generated filter or search URLs.

    It has been revealed that keep internal links pointed at the URLs you want crawled. Decide whether to block a parameter by what it does on your site; the presence of a query string alone is not a reason to disallow a page.

    Let’s say you have a lot of PDF documents, such as product guides, brochures, or downloadable papers, and you don’t want them crawled.

    Here is a simple robots.txt rule that will block search engine bots from accessing those documents:.

    The “Disallow: /*.pdf$” line tells crawlers not to crawl any URLs that end with .pdf.

    By using /*, the rule matches any path on the website. As a result, any URL ending with .pdf will be blocked from crawling. It will not match /guide.pdf?download=1 or an uppercase .PDF extension; test any such variants separately. If you want a PDF excluded from search, use an X-Robots-Tag: noindex HTTP header and keep it crawlable so Google can read the header.

    If you have a WordPress website and want to disallow PDFs from the uploads directory where you upload them via the CMS, you can use the following rule:.

    You can see that we have conflicting rules here.

    In case of conflicting rules, the more specific one takes priority, which means the last line ensures that only the specific file located in folder “wp-content/uploads/2024/09/allowed-document.pdf” is allowed to be crawled.

    Let’s say you have an API endpoint where you submit your data from the form. It is likely your form has an action attribute like action=”/form/submissions/.”.

    Sources indicate that if a crawler discovers the URL /form/submissions/, you may want to prevent crawling of that path. You can request that with this rule:.

    By specifying a directory in the Disallow rule, you are telling the crawlers to avoid crawling all pages under that directory, and you don’t need to use the (*) wildcard anymore, like “/form/*.”.

    Note that you must always specify relative paths and never absolute URLs, like “https://www.example.com/form/” for Disallow and Allow directives.

    Be cautious to avoid malformed rules. For example, using /form without a trailing slash will also match a page /form-design-examples/, which may be a page on your blog that you want to index.

    Read: 8 Common Robots.txt Complications And How To Fix Them.

    If you have an ecommerce website, you likely have directories that start with “/myaccount/,” such as “/myaccount/orders/” or “/myaccount/profile/.”.

    With the top page “/myaccount/” being a sign-in page that you want to be indexed and found by users in search, you may want to disallow the subpages from being crawled by Googlebot.

    You can use the Disallow rule in combination with the Allow rule to block everything under the “/myaccount/” directory (except the /myaccount/ page).

    And again, since Google uses the most specific rule, it will disallow everything under the /myaccount/ directory but allow only the /myaccount/ page to be crawled.

    Here’s another use case of combining the Disallow and Allow rules: in case you have your search under the /search/ directory and want it to be found and indexed but block actual search URLs:.

    Every website uses JavaScript, and many of these scripts are not related to the rendering of content, such as tracking scripts or those used for loading AdSense.

    Only block a script after confirming it is unnecessary for rendering the content and links you want indexed. Use URL Inspection to check the rendered page; blocking a shared bundle or a script with rendering dependencies can prevent Google from seeing key content. A robots.txt file on your host also cannot control a script fetched from a different host.

    Below is a sample line that is disallowing sample JavaScript, which contains tracking pixels.

    According to recent reports, you can block training bots while allowing AI tools to find your pages and retrieve them for users. The key is to give training, search, and user-requested AI crawlers separate rules.

    According to recent reports, publishers may block training to limit the use of their reporting without attribution, while ecommerce brands may welcome it if product mentions lead people to search and buy. Because the benefits differ by business, developers should set these rules with stakeholders.

    Disallowing training bots cannot guarantee that your content stays out of training datasets, because crawlers that ignore robots.txt can still collect it. It also does not force AI tools to visit or cite your site, as they may find the information elsewhere.

    Sources indicate that A BuzzStream study covered by SEJ in January 2026, found that 79% of the US and UK news sites examined disallowed at least one training bot, while 71% disallowed at least one retrieval or live-search bot. Because retrieval helps AI tools find and cite your pages, blocking those bots is a separate decision from opting out of training.

    OpenAI uses OAI-SearchBot to surface websites in ChatGPT search answers, while ChatGPT-User handles user-requested visits. Because search and training permissions are separate, you can allow OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User while blocking GPTBot.

    This example blocks OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s training crawlers while allowing their search and user-requested bots, along with Perplexity’s:.

    In the example above, /private/ is an excluded directory. Replace it with any paths you want to keep those bots from crawling.

    Most major AI crawlers follow robots.txt, including OpenAI’s GPTBot and Anthropic’s ClaudeBot.

    User-requested visits work differently because some providers allow their bots to bypass robots.txt or generally ignore it when acting on a user’s request. OpenAI notes robots.txt may not apply to ChatGPT-User, and Perplexity says Perplexity-User generally ignores it. Anthropic says its bots, including Claude-User, honor robots.txt. Because robots.txt only tells bots which URLs they may crawl, you need authentication to protect private content.

    The bot tokens and robots.txt policies for Copilot’s browser visits, Grok, DeepSeek, and Meta Muse remain unknown because I could not verify them in the providers’ public documentation.

    Google and Apple provide separate robots.txt tokens for controlling how crawled content is used:.

    Google-Extended covers Gemini training and specified grounding uses, where source content helps generate an answer. Blocking it does not block Googlebot or affect ordinary Google Search inclusion. Applebot-Extended controls foundation-model training without blocking Applebot’s search crawl. Neither token is a separate crawler, so these rules do not reduce crawling requests by themselves.

    After changing the file, check your server log files and confirm that your firewall allows the bots you want. Use server or CDN controls when you need to enforce access restrictions.

    For background, see SEJ’s earlier coverage of AI content use and AI chatbot traffic.

    Recent findings suggest that including your sitemap URL in the robots.txt file helps search engines easily discover all the crucial pages on your website. This is done by adding a specific line that points to your sitemap location, and you can specify multiple sitemaps, each on its own line.

    Unlike Allow or Disallow rules, which allow only a relative path, the Sitemap directive requires a full, absolute URL to indicate the location of the sitemap.

    Ensure the sitemaps’ URLs are accessible to search engines and have proper syntax to avoid errors.

    According to recent reports, the crawl-delay directive in robots.txt specifies the number of seconds a bot should wait before crawling the next page. While Googlebot does not recognize the crawl-delay directive, other bots may respect it.

    It helps prevent server overload by controlling how frequently bots crawl your site.

    For example, if you want ClaudeBot to crawl your content for AI training but want to avoid server overload, you can set a crawl delay to manage the interval between requests.

    According to recent reports, this requests a 60-second delay from ClaudeBot, which Anthropic documents as supporting the non-standard Crawl-delay extension. Use this when you intend to allow that crawl. Adding a delay does not override a Disallow: / rule for the same bot; review the complete group rather than copying both policies.

    Of course, there may be AI bots that don’t respect crawl delay directives. In that case, you may need to use a web firewall to rate limit them.

    Once you’ve composed your robots.txt, you can use these tools to troubleshoot if the syntax is correct or if you didn’t accidentally block an vital URL.

    Once you’ve updated your robots.txt, you must check whether it contains any error or accidentally blocks URLs you want to be crawled, such as resources, images, or website sections.

    Navigate to Settings > robots.txt to open the robots.txt report. It indicates the files Google fetched and any parsing warnings or errors. You can request a recrawl after a critical change. To test whether an individual page is blocked, use URL Inspection.

    The video below illustrates the report workflow; interface details may differ from the current version.

    Google’s robots.txt parser is an open-source parser and matcher based on the implementation used in Google’s crawler.

    It requires advanced skills to install and run on your local computer. But it is highly recommended to take time and do it as instructed on that page because you can validate your changes in the robots.txt file before uploading to your server in line with the official Google parser.

    In a recent development, robots.txt rules apply to the host, protocol, and port where the file is requested. If you need crawl restrictions on a subdomain, its robots.txt URL must serve the rules or redirect to a file that does; the parent domain’s file is not inherited.

    It creates challenges when you have a website with a dozen subdomains, as it means you should maintain a bunch of robots.txt files separately.

    However, it is possible to host a robots.txt file on a subdomain, such as https://cdn.example.com/robots.txt, and set up a redirect from https://www.example.com/robots.txt to it.

    You can do vice versa and host it only under the root domain and redirect from subdomains to the root.

    In a recent development, google applies the retrieved rules to the host that originally requested robots.txt, not automatically to the host storing the shared file. Configure a redirect from each host you want to manage, and check that the shared paths make sense for all of them.

    It helps make updates and maintenance more efficient. Otherwise, you would need to use a separate robots.txt file for each subdomain.

    Recent findings suggest that A properly optimized robots.txt file is crucial for managing a website’s crawl budget. It ensures that search engines like Googlebot spend their time on valuable pages rather than wasting resources on unnecessary ones.

    Blocking compliant crawlers can reduce unwanted requests. For AI systems, distinguish crawl restrictions from training-use controls, and verify the effect in your logs. Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended do not stop a separate crawler.

    Make sure you always validate your changes to avoid unexpected crawlability challenges.

    According to recent reports, however, remember that crawl demand and serving capacity both matter. Useful content, efficient page loading, and a healthy server remain vital alongside robots.txt rules.

    According to recent reports, OK, so Netflix failed to buy Warner Bros. Discovery.

    What if it bought NBCUniversal, tho?

    That potential acquisition is apparently top of wishlist for Netflix (and Variety already deemed it “Hollywood’s Next Major Deal”), but Comcast co-CEOs Mike Cavanagh and Brian Roberts say they’re not selling.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Sources indicate that well, according to Bloomberg, the current blueprint is for Netflix to revamp its approach to permanent interactive IRL installations, aka Netflix Houses. The streamer first unveiled these in 2023, with a demo setup that looked like someone stocked the gift shop in Jurassic Park with merch of the laser murder doll from Squid Game.

    At the time, Josh Simon, Netflix’s then-VP of Consumer Products (now CEO of collectibles company Funko) remarked the concept for Netflix Houses came from knowing “fans love to immerse themselves in the world of our movies and TV shows,” and “thinking a lot about how we take that to the next level.”.

    According to recent reports, netflix had flirted with pop-ups before that; those were mainly focused on selling stuff. Make no mistake, Netflix Houses are also focused on selling stuff, but in a Disney World kind of way, where fans pay $39 to enter the House and head through an art gallery-esque space filled with themed exhibits like exclusive theater shows, movie/TV set recreations, VR experiences, and arcade games. There are cafeterias and merch shops, but by and large the things to buy share billing with things to do.

    The Houses are permanent installations (for now just in Dallas and Philly, with one planned to open in Vegas in 2027) but the exhibits within rotate regularly to keep up with whatever’s trending on Netflix.

    This year, for example, the Houses were renovated to feature animated smash megahit KPop Demon Hunters. They’ve also spotlighted Stranger Things, One Piece, Wednesday, and the aforementioned Squid Game.

    Recent findings suggest that per Bloomberg, Netflix initially planned to open dozens of Houses across the U.S., focusing on quieter suburban areas away from downtowns. It wanted to snap up spaces in malls, which are not doing very well and might be willing to rent for cheap.

    But apparently the results from its first two Houses haven’t been quite what Neflix expected, so it’s pausing openings beyond Vegas until it can reassess.

    In a recent development, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg the Philadelphia location has daytime draws like mini golf and a movie theater, but doesn’t see much traffic at night. Dallas, meanwhile, is breaking even financially, and has done well with larger groups and corporate events.

    Netflix is also planning to see what comes from its Las Vegas location. Vegas, as you may know, is not in fact a quieter suburban locale–so if the House there proves to be profitable, with more traffic than Dallas and Philly, Netflix could reconsider where it opens in the future.

    People familiar with the matter noted Netflix is also looking at maybe taking Houses overseas. But wherever the next one ends up, it probably won’t open for at least another year, they said, until significant data from all three flagship U.S. locations is in.

    According to recent reports, now, with all this in mind, it’s worth remembering Netflix just shock-fired its longtime Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria and replaced her with Peter Rice, Disney‘s former General Entertainment Chairman. Film chief Dan Lin is out too. Clearly, Netflix hopes to revamp more than its IRL installations…and perhaps it’s hoping Rice’s Disney EXP comes in handy with the Houses?

    Tech Report: OpenAI Publishes Prompting Guidance For GPT-6.2 Astra via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, openAI is suggesting that developers who are migrating to GPT-6.2 Astra should revisit instructions such as “be concise” when they update their system prompts.
    • The company’s guidance for GPT-6 Astra says the model tends toward detailed, formatted responses.
    • GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol introduced Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, openAI is suggesting that developers who are migrating to GPT-6.2 Astra should revisit instructions such as “be concise” when they update their system prompts. The guide for developers on how to use GPT-6.2 states that Astra produces output that is more direct and brief by default than prior GPT models.

    The company’s guidance for GPT-6 Astra says the model tends toward detailed, formatted responses.

    GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol introduced Nov. 17. Developers can use both in the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol.

    Astra is described in the GPT-6.2 guide as “more concise and direct by default than earlier models,” with an adjustable overall tone that can range from a professional colleague to a more conversational assistant.

    In a recent development, the GPT-6.2 guide provides an example prompt for apps that use the model as a collaborator in day-to-day work. This prompt tells Astra to stick with the terminology of the user and its sources and to address the key points at the outset of its response.

    The GPT-6 guidance states, “GPT-6 Astra tends to use lists, tables and Markdown to make responses scannable.” The GPT-6 guide also contains an example prompt for apps that require prose with less formatting. This example prompt requests “clear, concise paragraphs” and directs the model to reserve lists for presenting parallel or sequential data.

    The GPT-5.6 guide states that GPT-5.6 is generally more concise by default than GPT-5.5, and that brevity instructions (such as “Be concise” and “Keep it short”) may be unnecessary for some types of task.

    Industry observers note that the GPT-6.2 guide advises asking the model to adjust for its target audience in emails, documents and any other writing intended for an external reader. It does this by suggesting a prompt which states that an external audience would probably have less understanding of the user’s context, so the model will need to provide the background information that audience needs.

    The prompt also provides guidance on editing by instructing the model to “preserve the author’s content and wording” when reviewing or editing existing work and adhere to the user’s direction as to what changes are to be made.

    According to recent reports, when performing longer tasks, the model can retain abbreviations, jargon or shorthand from the reasoning process, or from other agents, in its final answers. The guide suggests a method to address this by having the model write a self-contained response for anyone who hasn’t been tracking progress updates. Additionally, the guide’s example prompt tells the model not to include such shorthand, jargon or abbreviations in the response.

    Industry observers note that the guide notes GPT-6.2 Astra may propose a next step and wait for confirmation when a user’s intent is unclear. For work that can run on its own, the guide’s advice is to spell out the outcome the model should complete and which decisions need the user’s input.

    According to recent reports, the guide’s suggested prompts tell the model to make reasonable, reversible assumptions and keep working, stating what it assumed. It should stop and ask only when the task’s scope changes in a massive way, when it’s blocked, or when the user has to make a decision. It should also check in before irreversible or destructive actions.

    Sources indicate that the guide also points to an async question tool, which lets GPT-6.2 ask the user a question while it keeps working on anything that doesn’t depend on the answer. OpenAI’s async tool calling page says the app defines that tool and reveals the question to the user, and that it isn’t a built-in tool in the Responses API.

    It has been revealed that starting with GPT-6.2, the API will drop reasoning items as soon as it identifies that the client has made an edit to prior history, dropped down to a lower model version, or changed the end-user account or organization, according to OpenAI’s API documentation. Reasoning items provide the model’s reasoning from earlier in the conversation. Dropping these can lead to a reduction in answer quality and increase the number of tokens used by the model to repeat previous work.

    Recent findings suggest that examples on OpenAI’s page about the change include shortening a tool result, rewriting a developer message (which carries an app’s instructions), and replacing older turns with a summary. For new instructions, the page suggests appending a developer message that asks the model to ignore older instructions and follow the new ones, in place of editing the original.

    Recent findings suggest that teams building drafting or editing tools on GPT-6 Astra have prompts to review prior to migrating to GPT-6.2 Astra. Developers need to revisit any instruction that asks GPT-6 Astra to produce briefer answers, according to the 6.2 guide. Some of these tools may rewrite their own instructions as well during a conversation. This could lead to GPT-6.2 Astra losing its earlier reasoning, and spending additional tokens to recreate this process.

    Industry observers note that the GPT-6.2 guide calls its prompts a starting point, based on behavior seen with GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol. The GPT-6 guidance is still on the same page as the 6.2 guide, under its own tab, so teams can compare what each guide states about the model they’re moving from.

    Industry observers note that for reasoning effort, the 6.2 migration notes recommend medium for upcoming integrations and low for apps that are at the moment set to none or minimal. Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 guide, which I covered in September, also asked developers to retest effort settings carried over from Opus 5.

    Four and a half years after winning a Grammy for The Unofficial Bridgerton Musical, the songwriting duo known as Barlow & Bear has something upcoming in store for TikTok viewers.

    Sources indicate that abigail Barlow and Emily Bear are two of the creators behind To Die For Love, an 81-episode musical microdrama co-produced by TikTok and Ampersand. According to TikTok, the series follows “an ambitious half-witch vying for her coven’s crown. When she falls for a mortal, their romance takes an unexpected turn, forcing an impossible choice between family and the love of her life.”.

    Barlow & Bear created an original score for To Die For Love, while Barlow co-wrote the script alongside Oscar-nominated writer/director, actor, and opera singer Julia Aks.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Sources indicate that barlow also stars in the series opposite Broadway vet Derek Klena. Executive producers include Ampersand CEO Agnes Chu, Benj Pasek, Justin Paul, Danielle Perelman, Chris Crema, Matthew Ko, and Kevin Weaver.

    “Making To Die For Love has been one of the most rewarding creative experiences of our careers,” Barlow and Bear noted. “We love a pressure cooker, and building an entire musical in under five months proved that meaningful storytelling isn’t about time—it’s about the story and the people bringing it to life.”.

    Industry observers note that this isn’t the first creator-driven microdrama TikTok has brought to life. Earlier this year, Issa Rae’s media company, HOORAE, struck a deal with the platform to produce short-form web series for both TikTok and its companion app PineDrama. The first vertical series to emerge from that partnership, Screen Time, had racked up over 620 million views on TikTok and PineDrama as of late October, making it both platforms’ most-viewed show to date.

    TikTok doubled down on that success last month when it announced a fresh microseries-focused partnership with Made By Us Studios, which describes itself as a “first-of-its-kind, Hollywood-grade studio designed for the creator economy and powered by creator management company MADE BY ALL.”.

    Now, TikTok is forging ahead into the world of musical microdramas. To Die For Love will be available exclusively on TikTok and PineDrama, with all 81 episodes premiering December 21. The original soundtrack will be released by Atlantic Records.
